title: Don Byas, the all-around tenor
summary: He first saw Byas with Eddie Mallory's band, rates him unequaled as a tenor, and recalls Byas staying in Europe after the 1946 Redman tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you -- We didn't touch on Don Byas. When did you ever know Don Byas?
Don Byas? I knew Don Byas. He was from California. I first knew him when he came east with Mom Waters. She had an orchestra, and Eddie --

-- Eddie Mallory had the band. He had a great band. That's one of the first times I saw Don Byas. Of course, Don Byas had played with Bennie Carter before that, you see. But that's when I first heard him, and to this day I don't know anybody, to me, that is an all-around tenor player that was his equal. He had everything there was to have from a melodic standpoint. He could play fast as anybody that you ever heard. If you remember, he and Dizzy used to play them real fast unison things in 52nd Street in the bop era there that they used to play so fast together
I know you know about that.
And he went to Europe and stayed. He went to Europe with us with Don Redman in '46 when Don got that band together to go to Europe in '46, and Don Byas went over there then and never came back.
